source: RFC 0007 §7.3, §10.2 (control-typed-api decisions of 2026-11-22: no trust root through the service profile)
statement: No one is the trust root through the control API's service profile, on the service port or through the facade (CTL-58, CTL-65), for a tenant's document as for an app's: a change made or published through it is always analyzed, whoever is stated, and what the analysis cannot prove waits for a person, who approves on the operators' port. On that profile the caller's identity is only stated, by whatever workload the network admitted, so a trust root there would be anyone who names a platform administrator, and an app's catalog reaches every tenant at once. The trust root's exemption is a person's authority and belongs to the operators' port, where the gateway verified the credential. It is a fact of the request, the profile it came through, not of the identity: a forwarded identity on the operators' port stays eligible, and a change readied there is analyzed again when it is published through the service profile. The role class (CTL-79) still applies, and a removal that grants nothing still publishes alone.
guards: control:ServiceTrustRootTest#a stated platform administrator's widened catalog waits through the service port and the facade - CTL-81
control:ServiceTrustRootTest#a stated platform administrator's grant on a tenant's document waits through the service port - CTL-81
control:ServiceTrustRootTest#a holder's roles-only change still publishes through the service port, by the role class - CTL-81
control:ServiceTrustRootTest#a removal that grants nothing still publishes alone through the service port - CTL-81
control:ServiceTrustRootTest#the profile is the request's, not the change's, one readied on the operators' port waits when published on the service port - CTL-81
control:ServiceTrustRootTest#a stated tenant principal publishes alone what its stated roles hold, through the service port - CTL-58, CTL-81
